subject: computer-science
title: Overfitting, Splits and Decision Trees
welcome_lead: Why a model that aces training data can still fail.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: train/test split, overfitting, decision trees.
final_note: Generalisation is the goal — not memorisation.

concepts.def: When a model fits training data too closely and fails on new data.
When a model is too simple to capture patterns in the data.
Data used to fit a model.
Held-out data used only for final evaluation.
A model that splits data on feature thresholds at each node.
Splitting data into folds to estimate generalisation.

walkthroughs.body_html: Always hold back a test set never seen during training. A typical split is 80/20 or 70/30. Performance on the test set estimates how the model behaves on new data.
Overfitting: training accuracy high, test accuracy low. Underfitting: both low. Regularisation, more data, pruning and simpler models combat overfitting.
A decision tree picks the feature with the best split (highest information gain) at each node. Trees are interpretable but easily overfit — pruning or ensembling (random forest) helps.
